summary: 1. Sep 15 total production beat target by +14.1% (23,560 BCM) for a fourth straight daily beat, but ore production was zero against a 1,877.2 BCM target (-100%) — the worst single-day ore reading logged, extending the ore-miss streak that opened Sep 12 to four straight days; MTD total gap widened to +5.6%, MTD ore surplus narrowed to +51.0% (a target-base effect, not real recovery), and crusher stockpile throughput remains under a third of linear plan pace (30.8% MTD) after the heaviest single maintenance stop this cycle (9h45m). 2. 2. Fleet availability posted its best combined reading in several passes (87.49% daily, 80.63% core fleet) as EX-253's swing-bearing failure — standing since 28-Jul, tracked in every pass for 49 days — finally shows a close-out date, and two other long-standing faults (EX-327's hammer noise, WT-304's generator fault) both drop off the down-list entirely the same day; DZ-249 remains the one fault that does not resolve, now a second full day down. 3. 3. The survey gap reverses sharply negative (-29.9%, the worst since Sep 10) after three of the prior four days ran positive or near-flat, on a return of the three-excavator heap/overspill loading pattern; this pass's cross-check of the newly finalized day against the Client Meeting Report's own truck total surfaces new evidence that the whole `2609NN-INX-SUM` workbook family reports the *prior* calendar day rather than the file's own date — which would mean the 120th pass's closing "Day 21 (Sep 15)" section is actually Sep 14 data. 4. Flagged for a human check, not corrected retroactively. 5. Ore bottoming at zero on Sep 15 (after -8.7%, -26.5%, -67.0% on the three preceding days) is worth a direct check on which blocks are being worked — this reads more like a sequencing shift toward an all-waste phase than four independent misses. 6. Drilling missed its target for the first time in several days (-27.8%) the same day as the zero-ore reading, with no drill-rig fault logged in the Availability report — worth confirming whether it is linked to the same sequencing shift or a standalone rig/crew issue. 7. Two items outside this pass's dashboard scope are flagged for the next full-scope "compile mining operations KB" pass: a contact incident between SA-173 and SA-209 on the Mansourah 1 Main Ramp (16-Sep 05:30, Medical Treatment classification, no injuries, operators suspended pending investigation) in `Incidents report/`; and a site-leadership "ADW Re-Focusing Program" safety/productivity communication from Joe Coleman (new on site) to the full JRAR leadership team, cc Peter, in `Maintanance Shedules/`. 8. Both registered at index level only this pass. 9. The date-label question flagged above needs a direct human check against the original `260915-INX-SUM.xlsx` and `260916-INX-SUM.xlsx` files (both unedited in RAW) before any relabeling — see [[survey-volume-reconciliation]]'s Open Questions for the specific cross-check evidence.
